To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stress affects neurogenesis differently in males and females.
social support has different effects on neurogenesis in male versus female rats.
chronic stress and social housing affect the survival rate of newborn neurons in the dentate granular layer of the hippocampus differently in male and female Wistar rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of social housing on the stress-induced changes in cell proliferation in the DG of the hippocampus in both male and female rats.
the influence of stress and social housing on cell proliferation in the adult brain.
the effect of social housing and stress on neurogenesis in male rats and female rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stress and social housing conditions differentially affect neurogenic processes in male and female rodents.
chronic stress and social housing have differential effects on the survival of proliferative cells in the DG of male and female rats.
chronic stress and social housing affect neurogenesis in a sex- and time-dependent manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic stress has a negative effect on neurogenesis in male rats, whereas in female rats stress increases neurogenesis.
chronic stress and social housing affect neurogenesis in a gender-specific manner.
social housing can be a protective factor against the negative effect of stress in female rats, but not in male rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social support can be used in a therapeutic context to prevent stress-induced neurogenesis in both males and females.
social housing has a positive influence on the number of new neurons in both males and females.
social support is not always beneficial, as we found that social housing in male rats can have a negative effect on neurogenesis.
